amendments.normalized_body: In `update_molt_stress` (shrimp.rs:356), `(params.gh_min_d - gh_d) / params.gh_min_d` divides by `gh_min_d` without a `.max(0.01)` guard. Although invariant validation allows `gh_min_d == 0.0` via `check_non_negative`, making the branch unreachable in practice (since `gh_d < 0.0` cannot happen), the sister function `gh_mineral_factor` (line 1232) retains the `.max(0.01)` guard while `molt_mineral_modifier` (line 1247) does not. Either tighten the invariant to `check_positive` for `gh_min_d`, or add matching `.max(f64::EPSILON)` guards in `molt_mineral_modifier` and `update_molt_stress` for defensive consistency.

In `molt_cycle`, `failed_molt_accum` now scales with `failed_stage_count` (up to 3), meaning a single-day resolution can add up to 0.9 (was capped at 0.3). Similarly, recovery scales with `successful_stage_count` (up to 1.05 recovery in one day). This amplification is not documented as an intentional design change and may cause unexpectedly rapid population decline when all three life stages fail simultaneously. Add a brief doc-comment on the scaling rationale, and consider whether the per-stage multiplier should be dampened (e.g., `0.3 * failed_stage_count.min(2)`) to prevent a single bad day from being catastrophic.

Blocking: this patch does not implement `tanksim-6e5.5.6`'s geometry-scaling work. Geometry scaling still only changes dimensions and substrate nutrient stores in `crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:238-257`. The startup defaults that the bead calls out remain fixed: `startup_defaults_for_scenario()` still hard-codes shrimp counts per scenario in `crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:289-320`, `apply_startup_overrides()` still falls back to a fixed `200.0` LPH filter and never scales heater wattage in `crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:672-708`, and `build_plant_guilds()` still seeds every guild at `5.0` g in `crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:785-821`. `crates/tank_core/src/types/hardware.rs:64-91` also still carries the fixed `50.0` W heater / `200.0` LPH filter defaults. The actual edits are unrelated alkalinity-accounting changes in `crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:68-109`, `crates/tank_core/src/systems/nitrogen_cycle.rs:12-23`, and `crates/tank_core/src/systems/water_change.rs:131-152`, so the requested behavior and acceptance criteria around geometry-scaled hardware, plant biomass, and stocking are still unmet.

Robustness gap: the new alkalinity budget axis is not covered by the engine's invariant guard. `crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:68-109` makes alkalinity part of the canonical budget model, and `crates/tank_core/src/systems/water_change.rs:131-152` now emits explicit alkalinity deltas, but `crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:845-868` still validates only nitrogen and carbon before accepting a tick. That means an incorrect explicit alkalinity delta can pass `step_hours()` silently and only be caught if a caller happens to assert `Element::Alkalinity` separately. If alkalinity is meant to be first-class budget bookkeeping, the same guard that protects N/C should protect alkalinity too.
